parallel.requirements: Recognized the full five-layer benchmark obligation: Perses/PNF first, then Vulcan, PPR, LPR, Sivand, and run.sh wiring for bug1, bug2, bug3, and ppr_bug1.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used parallel subagents for Perses, PPR, LPR/Sivand design and audits while the parent coordinated final implementation and patch delivery.
parallel.implementation: Added Perses and PNF code, later Sivand/LPR/PPR wiring, and changed DD token reconstruction through render_tokens; PersesReducer requires a Grammar argument.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Committed requirement patches and delivered a final response claiming clean git state and full requirement coverage with run.sh exercising all experiment layers.
parallel.verification: Reported local unit tests and run.sh success, but official pytest later produced nine Perses errors plus two DD baseline failures.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official tests failed because PersesReducer() without arguments raises TypeError; DD also returned 75 tokens and 1348 tests instead of expected 64 and 1461.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same five requirements and dependency order, including full experiment coverage in run.sh and standard-library-only execution.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked without subagents; one agent owned investigation, implementation, integration, testing, commits, and final response across two rounds.
serial.implementation: Added experiments.py, PNF/Perses code, and later LPR/Sivand/PPR wiring; its PersesReducer also requires a Grammar argument.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a single integrated workspace with run.sh invoking reduction.experiments and final response reporting requirement patches for all covered layers.
serial.verification: Reported run.sh success and official pytest preserved the DD baseline, but all PersesReducer tests errored at setup.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final implementation still exposed the wrong no-argument PersesReducer API expected by the evaluator, causing the official both-fail result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run saw the full task: restore Perses first, then Vulcan, PPR, LPR, Sivand, and run.sh wiring for all named bugs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same prompt and the same dependency-ordered requirement set for all five benchmark layers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both later claimed complete coverage of all five requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run used multi-agent delegation, with round two reporting 12 spawn calls and child paths for LPR, PPR, Perses, and Sivand audit work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control disabled multi-agent execution and reported zero spawn calls and zero child activity in both rounds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel distributed investigation and audit work to children, while serial kept implementation and verification under the main agent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had multiple child work areas, but the retained record does not show a missing child brief, conflicting handoff, or interface contract gap causing the final evaluator failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegated child interface; it made the same public PersesReducer API mistake within one agent scope.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The known failing interface was the submitted PersesReducer constructor expected by tests, and both implementations exposed it as requiring grammar.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel added PNF/Perses code and changed DeltaDebugging to render through render_tokens, then constructed PersesReducer with a required Grammar parameter.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial added a separate experiments module and Perses reducer with the same required Grammar constructor, without the parallel DD rendering regression.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both broke the evaluator-visible Perses API; parallel also introduced a DD baseline regression by modifying the DD reconstruction path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The first parallel round timed out with child activity, then a second parallel round completed and delivered final workspace changes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial first round also timed out, and the serial second round completed without child results or delegation state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Timeout and retry occurred in both modes; parallel-specific child lifecycle did not leave a proven completed result unjoined or required failure untaken over.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated changes into the shared workspace and final patch set, including the DD/token rendering path that later failed baseline expectations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated a smaller set of changes and the evaluator shows the DD baseline tests passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only concrete integration regression unique to parallel is the DD behavior, but the evidence ties it to a code edit rather than a proven concurrent write or overwrite episode.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final response reported local unit tests and run.sh success, but official post-test failed on PersesReducer setup and DD baseline counts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final response reported run.sh success, and official post-test preserved DD while still failing PersesReducer setup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both accepted local evidence that did not cover the evaluator API contract; serial avoided the extra DD regression.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed substantially more agent work with multi-agent enabled, 12 round-two spawn calls, and higher token/tool counts, but still reached a final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no spawn calls and lower token/tool counts, and also reached a final response after two rounds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had higher coordination overhead, but the official both-fail outcome is explained by submitted code behavior, not by a budget-exhaustion label.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The completed official evaluations are not discordant: both modes failed. The shared decisive failure is that tests call PersesReducer() without a grammar, while both submissions define __init__(self, grammar). Parallel additionally regressed the DD baseline, but that did not create a different official pass/fail relation.
parallel_contributors: Shared Perses public API mismatch: PersesReducer requires grammar although the evaluator calls it with no arguments.
Additional ordinary parallel implementation regression: DD baseline produced 75 tokens and 1348 tests instead of expected 64 and 1461.
serial_contributors: Shared Perses public API mismatch: PersesReducer requires grammar although the evaluator calls it with no arguments.
Serial preserved the DD baseline, so its failure set is narrower than parallel but still unresolved.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel changed DeltaDebugging source reconstruction to render_tokens and failed DD baseline counts.
Serial organized experiment wiring through reduction.experiments and did not break the DD baseline.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference: both current official evaluations failed, and no parallel coordination pattern clears the retention gate
